simple.meaning: וָו (vâv) is a Hebrew word meaning “a hook (the name of the sixth Hebrew letter).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: וָו (H2053) appears 13 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 26:32, with occurrences in Exodus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to וָו (H2053) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in וָו (H2053) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: וָו (vâv) / H2053 is traced through Exodus 26:32, Exodus 26:37, Exodus 27:10, Exodus 27:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

structuredEvidence.definition: a hook (the name of the sixth Hebrew letter)

firstOccurrence.englishText: You shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold; their hooks shall be of gold, on four sockets of silver.

timeline.evidenceText: You shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold; their hooks shall be of gold, on four sockets of silver.
You shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia, and overlay them with gold. Their hooks shall be of gold. You shall cast five sockets of bronze for them.
Its pillars shall be twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze. The hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of silver.

Likewise for the length of the north side, there shall be hangings one hundred cubits long, and its pillars twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
All the pillars of the court around shall be filleted with silver; their hooks of silver, and their sockets of bronze.
He made four pillars of acacia for it, and overlaid them with gold. Their hooks were of gold. He cast four sockets of silver for them.
and the five pillars of it with their hooks. He overlaid their capitals and their fillets with gold, and their five sockets were of bronze.
their pillars were twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of silver.
For the north side one hundred cubits, their pillars twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
For the west side were hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
The sockets for the pillars were of bronze. The hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of silver. Their capitals were overlaid with silver. All the pillars of the court had silver bands.
Their pillars were four, and their sockets four, of bronze; their hooks of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals, and their fillets, of silver.

From the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels* A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 1775 shekels is about 17.75 kilograms or about 39 pounds. he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals, and made fillets for them.

definitions.short: a hook (the name of the sixth Hebrew letter)
definitions.full: H2053. vav [ וָו ] noun [masculine] hook, pin or peg (etymology unknown) — plural absolute וָוִים Exod 38:28 ; construct וָוֵי 27:10 5 t.; וָיֵיהֶם 26:32 5 t.; — only P, in description of tabernacle 26:32 , 37 ; 27:10-11 , 17 ; 36:36 , 38 ; 38:10-11 , 12 , 17 , 19 , 28 , the hooks or pegs of gold and silver, fastened on, or in, the posts of the tabernacle, to support the various hangings (curtains, screens, etc.) וזר (√ of following; compare Arabic bear a burden , or be guilty , yet see Fl in De Prov 21:8 ).
